judged_text: In sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse bypasses salesforceTokenSchema and zod's default strip behavior reduces accessTokenParsed.data to {access_token} (plus the injected sentinel), so the credential update persists {access_token, refresh_token} and drops instance_url, signature, id, issued_at, scope and token_type. After the first refresh in a sharing deployment the stored Salesforce credential has no instance_url, so every subsequent jsforce connection targets the wrong endpoint and the Salesforce integration breaks until the user re-authenticates — enabling sharing for any other app corrupts Salesforce credentials.

adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` it ignores the provided schema and instead uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`). That schema only defines `access_token` (the attempted “index signatures” are just computed literal keys, and zod objects strip unknown keys by default), so fields like `instance_url`, `signature`, etc. will be stripped from `data`. In `SalesforceCalendarService` the credential is then persisted as `{ ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }` (`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`), which in sharing+sync mode will drop `instance_url` and other required fields, corrupting stored Salesforce credentials after refresh.
